newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean ends up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean ends up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Friday on continued short-covering from retail investors, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at an intraday high of 3,160 yuan ($381) per tonne, rising 10 yuan. It opened at a low of 3,140 per tonne.
November was unchanged at 3,160 yuan, the January 1998 contract rose three to 3,135 and March was flat at 3,140 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 23,800 tonnes from 25,500 tonnes.
"The long-term outlook for soybeans is not optimistic because long position holders do not want to take physical goods," another trader said.
